latest_final: You are an HKU student with a course-selection deadline, but “course” in this story also means a dish or course in a meal. The deadline concerned choosing dishes for an HKU hall dinner, not academic classes. You personally chose those dishes in advance and then attended the evening hall dinner, where you ate the same dishes. Thus, in the literal meal sense, all “your courses” were gone in one evening: they had been selected and then consumed by you at the dinner. The apparent disappearance of your university courses was a wordplay on “courses,” not an actual enrollment or system failure.
